nomenclature.etymology_html:
- Combretum: From its resemblance to an undetermined climbing plant named in Latin by Pliny
- albidum: From the Latin albus which means white, referring to the pale colour of the lower side of the leaves

stem_bark.text: The bark of Combretum albidum is smooth and grey in colour. The branchlets are glabrous.
stem_bark.text_html:
The bark of Combretum albidum is smooth and grey in colour. 
The branchlets are glabrous.

seed.text: The seed of Combretum albidum is found at the centre of the 4 membranous wings. It is solitary, about 1 cm long, narrow in shape. It is light to dark brown in colour.
seed.text_html:
The seed of Combretum albidum is found at the centre of the 4 membranous wings. 
It is solitary, about 1 cm long, narrow in shape. 
It is light to dark brown in colour.

fruit.text: The fruits of Combretum albidum are ovoid in shape, with 4 membranous semi-circular wings. They are about 2 cm across. The fruits are green in colour, sometimes tinged with red, and turn brown when they dry. Each fruit has a single seed at the centre of its wings. The fruits are prominent over the canopy.
fruit.text_html:
The fruits of Combretum albidum are ovoid in shape, with 4 membranous semi-circular wings. 
They are about 2 cm across. 
The fruits are green in colour, sometimes tinged with red, and turn brown when they dry.
Each fruit has a single seed at the centre of its wings. 
The fruits are prominent over the canopy.

flower.text: The flowers of Combretum albidum are bisexual. They grow as panicled spikes at the end of the branches. The flowers are small, less than 1 cm, and tightly arranged on a peduncle which is 2 cm long. They are cream and green in colour with a pleasant smell. The flowers have 4 very small petals.
flower.text_html:
The flowers of Combretum albidum are bisexual. 
They grow as panicled spikes at the end of the branches. 
The flowers are small, less than 1 cm, and tightly arranged on a peduncle which is 2 cm long. 
They are cream and green in colour with a pleasant smell. 
The flowers have 4 very small petals.

leaf.text: The leaves of Combretum albidum are simple in an opposite arrangement. The leaves are oblong or ovate-lanceolate in shape. The leaves are about 5 to 8 cm long and 2 to 4 cm wide. They are thinly coriaceous. They are green in colour, paler on the lower side, and turn red before falling. The base of the leaf is cuneate-subcuneate, the leaf margin is entire and the leaf apex is acuminate. The petiole can be up to 1.5 cm long.
leaf.text_html:
The leaves of Combretum albidum are simple in an opposite arrangement. 
The leaves are oblong or ovate-lanceolate in shape. 
The leaves are about 5 to 8 cm long and 2 to 4 cm wide. 
They are thinly coriaceous. 
They are green in colour, paler on the lower side, and turn red before falling. 
The base of the leaf is cuneate-subcuneate, the leaf margin is entire and the leaf apex is acuminate. 
The petiole can be up to 1.5 cm long.

habit.text: Combretum albidum is a large woody deciduous liana that grows vigorously by winding itself against another plant. It can grow up to 10 m long. It can be a nuisance to its host as it can blanket the full canopy.
habit.text_html:
Combretum albidum is a large woody deciduous liana that grows vigorously by winding itself against another plant. 
It can grow up to 10 m long. 
It can be a nuisance to its host as it can blanket the full canopy.
